title: LRU Cache
description:
Implement an LRU (Least Recently Used) cache with a capacity limit.

Create a class `LRUCache` with:
- `__init__(capacity)`: Initialize with max capacity
- `get(key)`: Return the value if exists and move to most-recently-used. Return `-1` if not found.
- `put(key, value)`: Add/update key-value. If over capacity, evict the least recently used.
hint: Python's `collections.OrderedDict` is perfect — `move_to_end()` marks as recently used, `popitem(last=False)` removes the oldest.
outputExplanation: OrderedDict maintains insertion order. move_to_end() moves a key to the end (most recent), popitem(last=False) removes the first (least recent).

tests.name: Basic operations
tests.input:
cache = LRUCache(2)
cache.put(1, 1)
cache.put(2, 2)
print(cache.get(1))
cache.put(3, 3)
print(cache.get(2))

tests.name: Update existing
tests.input:
cache = LRUCache(2)
cache.put(1, 1)
cache.put(2, 2)
cache.put(1, 10)
cache.put(3, 3)
print(cache.get(2))
print(cache.get(1))
